info.title: Swarmail
info.description: Built for a program waiting on mail. Accepts any SMTP traffic on :1025, answers POP3 (RFC 1939 core + TOP/CAPA) on :1110 with the inbox as the maildrop, and exposes captured email through this API on :8025 — including MailHog/Mailpit-compatible read endpoints. Every accepted message is queryable immediately — there is no async gap where mail can be lost.

options.description: A guard-admitted OPTIONS is 405 with Allow: POST and no Access-Control-* header regardless of MCP-Protocol-Version (accepted decision 0043 §4). The modern invalid-header 400 rule is unmet for OPTIONS.

get.summary: No MCP SSE stream

400.description: Invalid MCP-Protocol-Version header

post.description: initialize, tools/list, tools/call. Supported revisions are 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25. This delivery claims version negotiation; full revision conformance is not claimed. The operator-chosen C1-C6 deviations remain documented in the [per-revision deviation register](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/swarmail/blob/main/specs/mcp-version-negotiation/reconciliation.md#exact-conflict-register). Single initialize echoes a supported proposal or returns 2025-11-25 for an unsupported string; omission retains March. Subsequent requests use MCP-Protocol-Version: the negotiated revision; absent header defaults to March. Invalid, duplicate or unsupported headers refuse HTTP 400/-32600/null after POST body/parse checks, also on other methods except OPTIONS, which stays 405 without CORS (decision 0043 §4). Every modern array refuses one -32600/null before effects. The stdio transport is available via `swarmail mcp`. Every error is a JSON-RPC error object (decision 0044 §1): malformed JSON or invalid UTF-8 is HTTP 400 -32700; a body over 2097152 bytes is HTTP 413 -32600 naming the limit; a value that is not an object is -32600 with a null id, once per such batch member; an object without an id is a notification that runs and gets no reply only when its method is a string — any other id-less object is -32600 with a null id (decision 0047 §3). A batch holds 1 to 16 members under 2025-03-26 only, polled concurrently: replies keep member order, member effects have no order. tools/call attempts share 1024 per server per monotonic second, including notifications and batch members; exhaustion is an isError text result before effects (notifications stay silent). Control and discovery remain available. Every tool refuses an argument key its inputSchema does not publish (-32602, additionalProperties: false). For 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 every tool declares an object-root outputSchema and each successful result includes structuredContent plus the same JSON text block; errors retain existing shapes without structured success data. March (including missing-version requests) preserves its thirteen existing catalogue entries and existing result bytes; discovery appends the two focused waits after them, fifteen in all. Explicit output projections pin the REST-backed MCP schemas to served OpenAPI; swarmail_wait_for_code and swarmail_wait_for_link (proposed decision 0094) are MCP-only, read-only and declare their own closed selected/ambiguous/timed_out variants, checked against independently stated expectations rather than OpenAPI. Dual output increases bytes/tokens and can exceed the unchanged 10 MiB stdio response cap where March text fits, yielding -32000; use smaller pages, though one large Email can still exceed it. Lost replies may follow committed mutations, without rollback or automatic replay. The operator owns tokens-per-success and invalid-argument/tool-misuse measurement, client receipts and the #151 baseline merge hold.

parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Without it the list is unchanged. `view=compact` answers the same `{total, emails}` envelope with the compact agent view of each email (the CompactEmail component): a handle, the headers, a snippet of at most 200 characters, codes, anchors with their text and an attachment list, and no bodies. `compact` is the only value; any other, the empty one included, is refused with 400 naming `view` (decision 0092 §4)

400.description: A blank inbox, an over-cap limit, a malformed value or an unknown query key (named). GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/messages accepts only the query keys to, from, subject, since_ms, limit and offset, plus view=compact (decisions 0048 §5, 0092 §4)

503.description: `storage commit failed` — the clear did not commit, nothing was removed (decision 0014); during shutdown the boundary refuses before any commit with the same text (decision 0024)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Any recipient, envelope included (see the list's `to`)

400.description: A blank inbox, a malformed value or an unknown query key, named — a count never paginates, so `limit` and `offset` are refused (decision 0048 §4)

get.summary: Long-poll until `count` messages match the filter (push-based wait, no sleep-polling)

parameters.name: no_findings_at_or_above
parameters.description: Qualify ordinary-filter matches whose successful report has no finding at or above this inclusive threshold. Empty findings qualify; failures abort with 503. Exact assert counts its snapshot including zero and never subscribes. Wait still requires one; qualify before paging. Zero timeout uses ready cached reports only; a required cold/busy report or incomplete scan at deadline is unavailable. A completed insufficient scan keeps the normal timeout/count.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Any recipient, envelope included (see the list's `to`)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size for the returned matches — the same domain list takes (decisions 0029 §1, 0030 §3): omitted is 100, 0 answers an empty `emails` array, above 250 refused with 400, never clamped. The wait still triggers at `count`; `limit` only bounds the page, so `count=120` with no limit returns 100 emails

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Matching messages to wait for; the answer carries the first `count` matches (newest first), at most `limit` of them. 0 is accepted and waits exactly like 1 — a wait never succeeds on an empty match set (decision 0010), so `matched` is then 1; above 250 refused with 400, never clamped (decision 0030 §3)

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Above 60000 the request is refused with 400, never clamped (decision 0018)

200.description: Matched — `total` is counted after the wait, describing the response's observed state (decision 0018)

400.description: `timeout_ms` above 60000 (decision 0018) or `count` or `limit` above 250 (decision 0030 §3) — refused, never clamped; a malformed value, a blank inbox, or an unknown query key such as `offset`, named — no waiter is registered (decision 0044 §3)

503.description: For a report predicate: deliverability analysis unavailable (capacity, cold/busy zero timeout, incomplete scan at deadline) or deliverability analysis failed (header/payload limits), with no partial count. Otherwise: The server is stopping — the wait answers `{"error":"shutting down"}` instead of parking (decision 0018)

get.summary: Assert an exact match count (200 when equal, 409 with expected/matched otherwise)

parameters.name: no_findings_at_or_above
parameters.description: Qualify ordinary-filter matches whose successful report has no finding at or above this inclusive threshold. Empty findings qualify; failures abort with 503. Exact assert counts its snapshot including zero and never subscribes. Wait still requires one; qualify before paging. Zero timeout uses ready cached reports only; a required cold/busy report or incomplete scan at deadline is unavailable. A completed insufficient scan keeps the normal timeout/count.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Any recipient, envelope included: `to=bcc@x&count=0` fails when the address was a Bcc envelope recipient — this is not a header-presence assertion

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Accepted and type-checked for parity with list (decisions 0029 §1, 0030 §3) — a negative or non-integer value is a 400 — but inert: no page default, page minimum or 250 cap applies, and every value answers the same assertion; the answer is a count, not a page

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Exact match count — 0 asserts the filtered inbox is empty; the count is never clamped to one, and exempt from the 250 page cap

400.description: A blank inbox, a malformed value or an unknown query key — a misspelled filter refuses by name instead of vanishing (decision 0044 §3); an assert never waits, so `timeout_ms` and `offset` are refused (decision 0048 §4)

503.description: deliverability analysis unavailable or deliverability analysis failed; no partial exact count

get.summary: Thread view of an inbox (newest thread first)
get.description: Mails are grouped into conversations by their References/In-Reply-To/Message-ID chains, falling back, for mail with no chain at all, to the normalized subject (leading Re/Fw/Fwd/Aw/SV/VS/Antw/WG/TR/RV/Odp/R/I/ENC/RES/Ответ/回复 markers stripped with an ASCII or full-width colon, whitespace runs collapsed, case-folded; a numbered Re[2]: stays literal). Each thread lists its mails oldest first. Capped at 200 mails.

400.description: A blank inbox, or any query key — the route takes none (decision 0048 §4)

get.summary: One thread by its key (the conversation, oldest first)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The thread's stable key, as returned by the threads list

400.description: A blank inbox, or any query key — the route takes none (decision 0048 §4)

get.summary: Live inbox feed (server-sent events)
get.description: One `threads` event per change, carrying the full thread view (the GET /threads shape) as JSON. The first event is the snapshot; a watcher that falls behind is repaired with a recomputed view, never an error. Subscribes before the first scan, so mail landing while the client connects is pushed, not missed.

400.description: A blank inbox, or any query key — the route takes none; refused before the feed subscribes (decision 0048 §4)

post.summary: Inject a synthetic email (full parse/extract pipeline runs)
post.description: Builds the fixture through the same seed constructor the MCP `swarmail_seed_email` tool uses (decision 0010). When `html` is given it is preserved verbatim under `Content-Type: text/html` and supersedes `text`; extraction (links, codes) runs at ingest. Envelope fields containing CR, LF or NUL are refused before anything is stored. POST /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/seed takes no query keys; any decoded key is refused with a native JSON 400 before seed construction or insertion. No query or a literal empty query preserves behavior.

400.description: Refused fixture — an envelope field (to, from or subject) contains CR, LF or NUL — or a body data error (an unknown key, a present null, a wrong type, a missing `to`, a non-object body) as `invalid seed body: …` naming the field (decision 0048 §2); nothing was stored. Malformed JSON keeps the extractor's plain-text 400, a non-JSON media type 415 and an oversized body 413. Any decoded query key is named in the native JSON 400. Body syntax, media, size and data-shape errors precede query validation; query validation precedes domain validation of a deserializable body.

503.description: `storage commit failed` — the commit refused, nothing was stored (decision 0012); during shutdown the boundary refuses before any commit with the same text (decision 0024)

get.summary: MailHog/Mailpit list shape over the whole store (Mailpit's summary envelope, newest first)
get.description: The Mailpit `/api/v1/messages` shape: {total, unread, count, messages_count, messages_unread, start, tags, messages}. No query names a mailbox: the whole store is one global mailbox, as both tools expose it. `?inbox=` scopes to a single swarmail inbox (a blank one is a 400); `?limit=`/`?start=` page. Each Snippet is built from at most the first 8192 bytes of its body; the page is built off the async workers.

delete.description: Body `{"ids":[...]}` — a non-empty array of message ids — deletes exactly those messages and replies `{"removed": n}`. Every other body (absent, empty, unparseable, wrong-typed, or an empty `ids` array) is answered `400` and deletes nothing; the cross-inbox wipe is `DELETE /api/v1/delete-all`.

get.summary: Lazy versioned deliverability report from immutable stored bytes
get.description: Closed empty query domain: every supplied query key refuses before lookup/evaluation. Off SMTP; swarmail-bulk/1 checks one-click structure, current RFC 5322 Message-ID and calendar-valid Date, genuine sender plain text, DMARC policy presence, From alignment and passing aligned DKIM-or-SPF. Missing trusted authentication evidence emits distinct error-level bulk.*.not_evaluated.v1 findings; sender headers cannot prove authentication. Every fix hint cites published Gmail/Yahoo and RFC sources. Text presence is advice, not equivalence; one-click structure does not prove DKIM coverage or endpoint operation. Obsolete-only identity/date syntax is unsupported by this checklist. demo.marker.v1 remains. Empty findings do not imply deliverability. Selected pre-removal reads may finish; new post-removal lookups fail. Process-local 128-slot Weak cache, four admitted blocking jobs, 8388608 raw bytes, 65536 per header block including separator, 262144 aggregate header bytes, 256 outer entities and depth 32 (root zero), at most 256 findings and 65536 compact JSON bytes; excess fails without truncation. No DNS or ambient time/network inputs.

400.description: Unknown or malformed query key

503.description: Fixed native JSON error: deliverability analysis unavailable or deliverability analysis failed. Failure is never an empty successful report.

get.summary: Current chaos rules

400.description: Any decoded query key is named in a native JSON error.

get.description: GET /api/v1/chaos takes no query keys. Any decoded key is refused with a native JSON 400 before reading the active configuration.

put.summary: Replace chaos rules (event: connect|mail_from|rcpt|data; probability 0-100; optional error line and delay_ms)

400.description: A well-shaped rule outside its shared domain is refused and never stored: probability 101 through 255 returns native JSON 400 with "probability must be an integer between 0 and 100"; an invalid SMTP reply line returns native JSON 400 with "error must be a single-line 4xx/5xx SMTP reply of at most 510 octets" (a 2xx code is refused); delay_ms above 300000 returns native JSON 400 with "delay_ms must be an integer between 0 and 300000". The active rules remain unchanged. Negative or omitted probability, null, wrong types, values above the field's u8 range, unknown event or rule keys and other JSON data errors use the extractor's plain-text 422. Malformed JSON is plain-text 400; unsupported media type is 415 and an oversized body is 413.

422.description: The JSON extractor's plain-text data error — negative, omitted, null or wrong-typed required probability; a probability value above the field's u8 range; a present null for error; an unknown event or rule key; or any other value that cannot deserialize. The active rules are unchanged.

400.description: Any decoded query key is named in a native JSON error before the configuration changes.

delete.description: DELETE /api/v1/chaos takes no query keys. Unsupported selectors such as `event=data` are refused with a native JSON 400 before clearing active rules.

get.summary: Current webhook targets (the secret is redacted: null)

400.description: Any decoded query key is named in a native JSON error. Stored credentials remain redacted.

500.description: Value-free response preparation failure: {"error": "webhook response preparation failed"}

503.description: CA admission unavailable (capacity, charged bytes, contention, closed scope or failed facility): webhook CA preparation unavailable. No configuration change.

get.description: GET uses awaited off-worker response preparation; a worker join failure returns the fixed value-free 500 webhook response preparation failed. The targets redacted (decisions 0041 §3 and accepted 0067): every secret is null and every URL loses its userinfo (http://user:pw@host/x is shown as http://host/x; delivery still sends the credentials). ca_pem contains only canonical certificate blocks whose complete reconstructed bundle loads through the delivery TLS builder; unrelated PEM sections and prose are omitted, while DER, order and duplicates are preserved. A supplied unprojectable bundle is an empty string; absent ca_pem is null. Admission and installed input are unchanged. PUT is the only writer and an operator retains their own payload. GET /api/v1/webhooks takes no query keys; any decoded key is refused with a native JSON 400 before reading targets. Server-managed preparation uses two process-wide dedicated native workers, no pending queue, and a 64 MiB logical charged-job budget. Oversized valid input can refuse; admission has no fairness guarantee.

put.summary: Replace webhook targets. Each delivery POSTs {event:"received", email:{...}} with X-Swarmail-Secret; retried 4x (100ms..1.6s). http:// and https:// targets (https over TLS via reqwest + rustls, verification on; optional per-target ca_pem), dialed directly: environment proxies are ignored and redirects are not followed. The 200 echo is redacted like GET. GET projection and PUT validation/echo preparation run on awaited dedicated native CA jobs; a join failure is a value-free 500.

503.description: CA admission unavailable (capacity, charged bytes, contention, closed scope or failed facility): webhook CA preparation unavailable. No configuration change.

200.description: The installed list, redacted like GET

500.description: Value-free webhook preparation failure; no PUT replacement occurred

400.description: A target that cannot be delivered is refused before any effect (issue #47, decision 0029 §5): the body names the defect, e.g. "webhook target 0: webhook URL must name a host" (a scheme-forgotten localhost:9000), an unsupported scheme, an unparsable URL, a blank or control-bearing inbox, a ca_pem any of whose certificates does not load into the delivery client (decision 0048 §1), or a secret that is not an HTTP header value of at most 4096 octets without leading or trailing space or tab (decision 0041 §1). A body data error — an unknown key, a present null, a wrong type, a missing url, a non-array body — is `invalid webhooks body: …` naming the path and the JSON kind (decision 0048 §2). No refusal echoes the secret, the URL or a supplied value. Nothing is applied: the previous target list stays in place. Malformed JSON keeps the extractor's plain-text 400, a non-JSON media type 415 and an oversized body 413.
Any decoded query key is named in a native JSON error before targets change.

delete.description: DELETE /api/v1/webhooks takes no query keys. Unsupported selectors such as `inbox=a` are refused with a native JSON 400 before clearing targets.

GuardRefused.description: Refused before the router by the whole-plane Host/Origin guard, on every route and method (decisions 0030 §2, 0043): on a loopback bind, a Host that is not a loopback spelling of the bound port, or a present Origin that is not one; off loopback, a present Origin that does not name the request's own Host authority. `{"error": …}` naming the refusal

BodyTooLarge.description: The request body is over the REST plane's 2097152-byte (2 MiB) limit: the JSON extractor's own plain-text refusal (`Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded`), nothing applied. `POST /mcp` answers its 413 as a JSON-RPC error object instead

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request does not declare `Content-Type: application/json`: the JSON extractor's own plain-text refusal, nothing applied

DeliverabilitySeverity.description: Inclusive threshold order: info < warning < error

occurrence.description: Zero-based occurrence; null for a missing field

path.description: Structural child indexes in wire order, root []; message/rfc822 root is child 0

part_path.description: Structural child indexes in wire order, root []; message/rfc822 root is child 0

byte_offset.description: First URL source byte in transfer-decoded payload before charset/entity decoding; no URL is echoed

DeliverabilityReport.description: At most 65536 compact JSON bytes; ordered by rule id, typed location, severity, hint; exact duplicates removed. Rule meaning/parser/location/hint/order changes require a new rule-set id. demo.marker.v1 reads the first X-Swarmail-Demo value, unfolded and space/tab trimmed: info, warning or error emits one fixed header finding. Seven bulk checklist rules also ship (proposed 0089). Pass emits no row; authentication unknown emits a distinct not_evaluated error, so no production message currently qualifies at any predicate threshold.

envelope_from.description: The SMTP MAIL FROM reverse path, captured at ingest: "" for a bounce's null sender <>, null only for mail stored before it was kept — never backfilled from the header From (decision 0044 §8)

recipients.description: The envelope recipients (RCPT TO), Bcc included; the `to` filter matches these as well as the To/Cc headers

codes.description: Likely OTP/verification codes (4–10 ASCII digits), extracted at ingest: at most the first 64 distinct, in extraction order (decision 0049); a row stored before the cap keeps its array verbatim

message_id.description: The Message-ID header value, angle brackets stripped; absent when the mail has none

in_reply_to.description: The first In-Reply-To id; absent when the mail has none

references.description: The References ids in header order; absent when the mail has none

key.description: Stable short key (16 hex chars) usable in URLs and the thread endpoint

subject.description: The subject, as stored (not normalized), of the oldest mail in the thread that has one — oldest by receive time, then id, within the view's newest 200 mails; a later reply's subject never replaces it. Optional and never null: the key is absent when no mail in the thread has a subject

CompactEmail.description: The compact agent view of one email (decision 0092): what an assertion needs and no body. Fetch the whole email by `id` with GET /api/v1/messages/{id}. Optional members are omitted, never null, except `attachments`, which is null for mail stored before attachments were captured.

id.description: The handle: the id of GET /api/v1/messages/{id}

snippet.description: The text part, else the HTML rendered to text, from at most the first 8192 bytes of the body, whitespace runs collapsed, at most 200 characters, `...` appended when the output or the source was cut

codes.description: The stored codes, uncapped; omitted when empty

anchor_text.description: null when the label is unknown

anchors.description: Every link occurrence in ingest order, at most 250; omitted when empty and for mail stored before link occurrences were kept (those carry `links`)

anchors_total.description: The exact occurrence count, present only when `anchors` was cut at 250

links.description: The stored URLs of mail stored before link occurrences were kept; omitted otherwise

size.description: The decoded part length in bytes

attachments.description: The attachment parts of the message in parser order, at most 250; omitted when the mail has none; null when unknown

attachments_total.description: The exact attachment count, present only when `attachments` was cut at 250

SeedRequest.description: Fixture body. `html` is preserved verbatim and supersedes `text` when both are given. `to`, `from` and `subject` refuse CR, LF and NUL. An omitted optional field takes its default; a present null, a non-string or an unknown key is refused with 400 naming the field (decisions 0044 §3, 0048 §2). The stored mail's envelope_from is the seed's from.

from.description: Defaults to fixture@swarmail.dev; refuses CR, LF and NUL

to.description: The recipient envelope address; refuses CR, LF and NUL

subject.description: Defaults to (no subject); refuses CR, LF and NUL

text.description: Plain-text body; ignored when html is given

html.description: HTML body, preserved verbatim under Content-Type: text/html; supersedes text

probability.description: Percentage chance the event fires. The shared domain is the integer range 0–100. Values 101 through 255 are domain refusals with native JSON 400: probability must be an integer between 0 and 100. Negative, omitted, null, wrong type and values above 255 fail extraction with plain-text 422. A null event clears that event; it is not a probability value (decisions 0025, 0048).

error.description: Optional SMTP reply line; omission uses the stage's default. It starts with three ASCII digits whose first digit is 4 or 5. If any bytes follow the code, byte four is ASCII space; bare codes and a trailing space are legal. No CR or LF. Maximum 510 UTF-8 octets, including all bytes of non-ASCII text and excluding the CRLF appended on the wire. Supplied null is refused with 422 (decisions 0029, 0044).

delay_ms.description: Optional delay in milliseconds; omission defaults to 0. Values above the 300000 ms stage-timer ceiling are refused, never clamped (decision 0029).

ChaosConfig.description: A null event clears that event's rule. Omitted events remain unset when REST replaces the whole configuration.

WebhookTargetRequest.description: One PUT target. The key set is closed and an optional string is omitted or a string, never null (decision 0048 §2); omit `inbox` for every inbox.

url.description: Must parse with an http:// or https:// scheme and a host to dial — refused at PUT otherwise (localhost:9000 is read as scheme localhost and is refused). Userinfo is sent as Basic authorization and stripped from every echo and log line

inbox.description: Fire only for this inbox; blank or control-bearing names are refused

secret.description: An HTTP header value the delivery client accepts: at most 4096 octets, no control characters but tab, no leading or trailing space or tab

ca_pem.description: PEM of one or more extra root CAs to trust for this target, on top of the built-in root store. Every certificate must load into the delivery client at PUT, at least one — loadability only, not a promise that a handshake succeeds (decision 0048 §1). Unrelated PEM sections remain ignored by admission.

WebhookTarget.description: A target as GET and the PUT echo show it: the secret withheld (null), URL userinfo removed, an absent inbox or ca_pem null. A diagnostic, not a PUT template (decision 0048 §3).

url.description: Must parse with an http:// or https:// scheme and a host to dial — refused at PUT otherwise (localhost:9000 is read as scheme localhost and is refused). Userinfo is sent as Basic authorization and stripped from every echo and log line

secret.description: An HTTP header value the delivery client accepts: at most 4096 octets, no control characters but tab, no leading or trailing space or tab; GET /api/v1/webhooks redacts it — PUT is the only writer

ca_pem.description: Canonical validated certificate-only projection of the configured PEM. DER, order and duplicates are preserved; unrelated sections/prose are omitted. If the supplied bundle cannot be fully projected, this is an empty string; absent remains null. Diagnostic output, not original input.
